request.spec:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.
request.prompt:

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Delete and restore for DRAFT claims are in. With `bin/e2e`, 3 of the 4 tests pass, including the main "delete and restore draft" test. The 4th, "scenario 3", fails because of a mistake in the spec itself, not the app.

**The scenario 3 failure:** the test sets the sheet's parent to `${sheet}-p`, but at lines 1145 and 1228 it expects the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`, a placeholder that was never filled in. The app correctly shows the real value (e.g. `smvk1ag3gyqzl-p`). I'm not allowed to edit the spec, and making the app print `__SHEET__` would be wrong. To check everything after those lines, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with just that placeholder filled in, and scenario 3 then passed. I deleted the copy afterwards, so the spec folder is unchanged. Someone who can edit the spec will need to fix those two lines.

**What changed:**
- **New status:** claims can now be `DELETED`. A deleted claim isn't counted anywhere: not in any total, and not in the status counts in the header or the summary, which only list the existing five statuses. Its status column already had room for the new value, so no database change was needed.
- **Delete:** only a DRAFT can be deleted. Any other status, or a claim falling in a closed period, is refused with an error on the claim. A deleted claim can't be edited, opened or voided, because those already work only from the allowed statuses.
- **Restore:** turns a deleted claim back into a DRAFT, but only on the same sheet-today it was deleted (checked against the DELETED line in its log). On a later day it is refused.
- **Log and audit:** each change adds a `DELETED` or `DRAFT` line to the claim's log and writes `CLAIM_DELETED` or `CLAIM_RESTORED` to the audit file, in the same format as the other claim events.
- **Screen:** each claim row has new Delete and Restore buttons.

The rules are in `claim/ClaimStatus.java`, `claim/ValidateClaimStatus.java` and `claim/ClaimStatusChange.java`. The front-end changes are in `features/claims/claims.ts` and `claims.slot.tsx`.

**Closed periods:** whether a claim is in a closed period is decided by its due-by date, as for the app's other claim actions, not by its claim date. That's why the claim dated 2026-02-05 in the closed P1 period can still be deleted, which the test expects.
